title: memory-org
description: Use this when you need an agent that organises or retrieves memories scoped to a project or organisation.

title: researcher
description: Use this when you need to discover, grade, and catalog third-party tools/patterns/use cases before building — sweeps registries and the web via the search MCP, grades sources, writes per-finding memory episodes (agent:approved/agent:blocked), and returns a build-vs-integrate verdict.

title: test-runner
description: Use this when you need an agent that runs test suites and reports results.

title: sox-memory (graph memory subsystem)
description: Use this when you want the full sox-memory graph-memory subsystem installed in one command — expands to memory-server (MCP tools, stdio, with in-process deterministic batch enrichment), memory-flush (SessionEnd hook), memory-cli (store lifecycle commands), and memory-usage (how-to skill). Fully deterministic; zero LLM calls; no provider required.

title: Memory CLI
description: Use this when you need to manage the sox-memory store from the shell — provides memory init|status|list|registry subcommands for store lifecycle, scope selection, and registry inspection. Fully deterministic; zero LLM calls.

title: Memory Session Flush
description: Use this when you need session memory durably persisted at conversation end and scope promotions reviewed — binds SessionEnd (persists working memory, enqueues episodes, nudges memoryd) and ScopePromotionProposed (runs promotion approval policy). Deterministic; zero LLM calls.

title: Agent Memory Server
description: Use this when an agent needs durable, searchable memory across sessions — exposes 7 memory_* tools over a single-file SQLite graph store with hybrid recall (vec+BM25+temporal, <50ms, zero LLM), write-enqueue, session state, community lookup, and bi-temporal invalidation.

title: Using the soxe memory system
description: Use when an agent should recall prior knowledge or store durable findings in the soxe graph-memory system via the memory_* MCP tools (memory_recall / memory_write / memory_search_entities / memory_invalidate).

title: dep-inject
description: Use this when you need a slash command that demonstrates dependency injection patterns.

title: TokenGuard Pseudonymizing Proxy
description: Generalized pseudonymizing HTTP proxy. Tokenizes PII in outbound API requests and detokenizes inbound responses — provider-agnostic via pluggable adapters. Seeded identifiers are mapped bijectively and never reach the wire.

title: demo-creator — generate a project's DEMO.md acceptance script
description: Use this skill to produce a project's demo script / DEMO.md / acceptance walkthrough / QA verification doc that both tells the product story like a live demo AND functions as a rigorous acceptance test. Turns a project spec (or PRD/README/landing copy/code) into a persona-narrated, presentation-grade DEMO.md with exact commands, exact data, binary pass/fail assertions, full happy/edge/recovery coverage, requirement->capability traceability, and a tracked UNRESOLVED.md ledger for any guessed interface.

title: di-codex
description: Use this when you need a skill that demonstrates dependency injection for Codex-based workflows.

title: dep-injector
description: Use this when you need a skill that demonstrates dependency injection for Claude-based workflows.

title: forbidden-access
description: Use this when testing permission enforcement — this skill targets a forbidden host path and must be rejected.

title: Iterative Research Refinement — meta-cognitive research process
description: Use this when you need to research a question, produce findings, audit your own process, and iteratively refine the methodology — not just the answer. A meta-cognitive research process (v9) that improves itself through nested feedback loops: Position Declaration, Iteration Manifest with quantified baselines and MANDATORY runtime metrics, Pre-Commitment, Observation Generalization, Loop 1 research, Loop 2 process audit, Loop 3 propose-to-new-file, Loop 3a fresh-subagent real-execution test with runtime measurement, Loop 3b commit, Loop 4 verification.

title: sox-ingest — Ingest external sources into sox-ecosystem
description: Use this when you need to port an external repo, file, or directory into sox-ecosystem as born-conformant extensions. Encodes the full ingestion flow: initialize -> generalize+author -> validate -> publish -> install -> enable -> remove-old, delegating per-type and per-operation specifics to references/. An agent told 'ingest <source> into sox' loads this skill and runs the complete flow with no bespoke prompts.

title: TUI & CLI Design — design and build professional terminal interfaces
description: Use this when designing or building clean, professional, minimal terminal UI (TUI) applications and command-line tools. Covers full-screen TUIs (file managers, dashboards, monitors, git/k8s tools, REPLs), interactive CLI prompts, and simple command-line utilities. Includes per-ecosystem deep-dives (Go/Bubble Tea, Rust/Ratatui, Python/Textual, TypeScript/Ink), visual and interaction pattern references, exemplar app analysis, and universal TUI design principles. Harvested from gfargo/skills v1.4.0.

title: soxe CLI
description: LLM extension ecosystem CLI — extension #0 (D1/D2 self-hosting)
